title: A non-own Action that declares targetEntity anyway, and the reference does not resolve
target: AZ7 / scope of the targetEntity reference rule
why: The Action is evaluated at 'organization' scope and declares targetEntity 'Gadget', which no entity in this manifest declares. VALIDATOR-AZ7 item 5 settles this: 'targetEntity is optional outside own and carries no scoping semantics there ... Where it is present it must still satisfy items 1 and 2.' Item 1 requires that exactly one declared entity carry that name. Zero matches is a failure, so this manifest is rejected. The reason it matters is latency of harm rather than immediate harm: a dangling reference tolerated on a non-own Action becomes live the moment somebody changes that Action's scope to 'own', and the change passes review because the field was already there and already looked correct.
notes: VALIDATOR OBLIGATION, NOT A SCHEMA ONE. The check is the same cross-array join as az7-n2 and is not expressible in draft 2020-12; the schema will and should ACCEPT this document, and that accept is not a schema defect. PROVENANCE, KEPT DELIBERATELY: this case was authored as an OPEN QUESTION with expectedOutcome UNDECIDED, because AZ7 as originally stated to QA constrained 'own' only and said nothing about non-own Actions carrying targetEntity. Three readings were defensible and disagreed. AUTHORIZATION_STANDARD.md §4.1 VALIDATOR-AZ7 item 5 subsequently decided it, and this fixture's expectedOutcome was set from that recorded decision — NOT from observed behaviour, and NOT from QA's own preference, though the decision did match the reading QA recommended. If item 5 changes, this expectation changes with it and not otherwise.
